text:
Sam: heads up — saw a hot handback failover today that coincided with an eviction. client observed a read-after-write for a short-lived prefix. throwing this into channel to record details and next steps.

Mia: ugh. timeline? any logs or event ids?

Sam: quick timeline —
- 12:05:12 handback initiated (node A -> node B)
- 12:05:13 failover path taken (node A dropped)
- 12:05:14 eviction job cleaned prefix X (hot)
- 12:05:15 client read returned stale empty list then later got data back on retry

Oliver: can you paste the eviction + handback snippets? curious if eviction used hard-evict or soft window.

Sam: log snippets:
```
[12:05:13] HANDOFF_START prefix=X lease=0x7f3a
[12:05:14] EVICT prefix=X policy=hard reason=mem_pressure token=42
[12:05:15] READ prefix=X -> [] (no-resident)
[12:05:16] HANDOFF_COMPLETE prefix=X -> node=B
```

Jen: so looks like the handoff overlapped with a hard evict. that's a problematic interleaving — we rely on the lease token to prevent races but failover timing can make token checks miss.

Mia: do we have a guard that prevents hard-evict when a handoff is in-flight? I thought we had soft-evict grace credits for hot prefixes.

Oliver: soft-evict exists but only applied when prefetched==true AND recent-access > threshold. This prefix was in hot rotation but eviction policy outran the hotness metric because of a lagged telemetry update.

Sam: client retried and eventually got data after the handoff completed and node B rehydrated prefix. no data lost, but R/W latency spike + potential correctness hazard if writes had been in-flight.

Jen: action items suggestion:
- short term: treat handoff as a blocker for hard-evict for N ms (quiesce window)
- medium: add a handoff-bit to residency metadata so evicts check (evict_allowed = !handoff_in_flight)
- long term: make eviction idempotent with lease epoch compare and read-repair path so reads always check remote store when local miss happens during recent handoff epochs

Mia: +1 for adding handoff-bit. cheap and fast to roll out. also add debug metric "evict_during_handoff" and a trace tag.

Oliver: caveat — adding handoff-bit increases arbitration complexity for the evict controller. it needs to subscribe to handoff events and keep a small LRU of recent prefixes to avoid unbounded memory. doable.

Sam: also proposing to tweak the hard-evict backoff to check last-handshake-ts and last-prefetch-access; if last-handshake < X ms, skip hard-evict. simpler than full handoff-bit and covers most cases.

Jen: that will reduce incorrect hard-evicts but doesn't solve stale token races where two nodes think they own the prefix. for that we need a cheap epoch CAS on eviction: evict only if lease_epoch == observed_epoch.

Sam: agreed. short-term safety patch: implement N ms handoff quiesce + metric + revert to soft-evict if uncertain. medium-term: handoff-bit + eviction CAS. long-term: read-path repair to consult fallback store on local miss when last-handshake < threshold.

Mia: who wants the short-term patch? I can take it, will add metrics and a canary.

Oliver: I'll draft the medium-term design for the handoff-bit and eviction CAS. include a memory cap and eviction controller subscription design.

Jen: I'll put together the read-repair plan and the test harness for a simulated failover+evict chaos test.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary job created by Mia for "soft-evict-quiesce-726543" -> rolling to 3 nodes in staging at 14:00 UTC. :rocket:

Sam: awesome. also note to ops: monitor client 5xxs and read-latency spikes for the next 6h. i'll follow up with a mini-postmortem if we see it reproduce.

Mia: logging doc link: https://internal.redwood/ops/evict-handoff-guidance (I'll update after canary) :memo:

Oliver: one last thought — we should add a small unit test that simulates handoff + concurrent hard-evict in the library so future refactors don't remove the check.

Sam: agreed. quick PRs incoming. thanks all :thumbsup:
